passages.note: Bill overview page lists Kavanagh as a co-sponsor of HB2853.
House Third Reading vote page shows Kavanagh voting Y on final passage, 31-26 (not near-unanimous).

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Enacted bill text (single-subject, signed by the Governor) adds a new class of qualified student covering nearly all students, matching rung 5's universal eligibility clause.

rows.reasoning: Kavanagh co-sponsored and voted Yes on final passage of HB2853 (2022), a single-subject Arizona empowerment scholarship accounts bill whose enacted text adds a new 'qualified student' class covering any resident eligible to enroll in a public preschool, kindergarten, or grades one through twelve who does not otherwise qualify, effectively opening the ESA program to nearly all students. This matches the rung text 'Providing universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school ... chosen by the family.' Although the act predates his 2023 Senate term, it is from his prior House term in the same legislature, so it counts as in-term (V5 ruling 2026-09-27, option B).
